questions.stem: Mahatma Gandhi began the famous Dandi March to break the salt law on:
questions.explanation: Gandhi started the Dandi March (Salt March) from Sabarmati Ashram on March 12, 1930, with 78 followers. After a 24-day, 385 km march, he reached Dandi on April 5 and made salt by boiling sea water, launching the Civil Disobedience Movement.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The Quit India Movement was launched by the Indian National Congress on:
questions.explanation: The Quit India Movement was launched at the Bombay session of the INC on August 8, 1942. Gandhi gave the slogan 'Do or Die' (Karo ya maro), demanding an immediate end to British rule. British authorities arrested Gandhi and top leaders that very night.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre, in which General Dyer ordered firing on a peaceful crowd, occurred on:
questions.explanation: On April 13, 1919 (Baisakhi day), General Reginald Dyer ordered troops to fire on a large unarmed crowd gathered at Jallianwala Bagh, Amritsar. Hundreds were killed and thousands wounded. The massacre shocked the nation and intensified the freedom movement.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: Mahatma Gandhi's first Satyagraha in India (1917), fighting for the rights of indigo farmers against British planters, was at:
questions.explanation: Gandhi's first Satyagraha in India was the Champaran Satyagraha (1917) in Bihar, where he organized peasants against the tinkathia system forcing farmers to grow indigo. It was the first application of the Satyagraha method on Indian soil.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The 'Surat Split' of 1907 divided the Indian National Congress into two factions led by:
questions.explanation: The Surat Split (1907) was between the Moderate faction led by Gopal Krishna Gokhale (seeking reforms through constitutional means) and the Extremist faction led by Bal Gangadhar Tilak (demanding Swaraj/self-rule through mass agitation). The split weakened the Congress for a decade.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The Lucknow Pact (1916) was a historic agreement between:
options: Indian National Congress and the Muslim League
questions.explanation: The Lucknow Pact was signed between the INC (led by Tilak) and the Muslim League (led by Muhammad Ali Jinnah) in December 1916. It was a joint scheme of constitutional reforms and a landmark in Hindu-Muslim unity — subsequently undermined by the Khilafat aftermath.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: Which repressive British legislation of 1919 allowed detention of political activists without trial and directly sparked mass protests including the Jallianwala Bagh gathering?
questions.explanation: The Rowlatt Act (officially the Anarchical and Revolutionary Crimes Act, 1919) empowered the government to arrest and detain individuals without trial or judicial review. Gandhi organised a nationwide hartal (strike) against it; the Jallianwala Bagh gathering on April 13 was a peaceful protest against it.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The Nagpur Session of the INC (1920) was significant because it formally adopted the programme of:
questions.explanation: The Nagpur Session of the INC (December 1920) formally adopted Gandhi's Non-Cooperation Movement programme — boycott of legislative councils, courts, government educational institutions, and foreign goods. It also reorganised the Congress on linguistic lines.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The first individual Satyagrahi chosen by Gandhi to launch the Individual Satyagraha (October 1940) against India's involvement in World War II was:
questions.explanation: Acharya Vinoba Bhave (later famous for the Bhoodan Movement) was selected by Gandhi as the first individual Satyagrahi to deliver the anti-war message. Nehru was the second. The movement was symbolic and low-key, unlike mass civil disobedience.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The Gandhi-Irwin Pact (March 1931) led to the suspension of which movement?
questions.explanation: The Gandhi-Irwin Pact was signed between Gandhi and Viceroy Lord Irwin on March 5, 1931. Under it, Gandhi agreed to suspend the Civil Disobedience Movement and participate in the Second Round Table Conference. The British agreed to release political prisoners and allow salt collection near the sea.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, and Rajguru were executed by the British at Lahore Central Jail on:
questions.explanation: Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev Thapar, and Shivaram Rajguru were hanged at Lahore Central Jail on March 23, 1931 for the killing of British police officer John Saunders in 1928. March 23 is now observed as Shaheed Diwas in India.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The Simon Commission (1927) was boycotted by Indians across the political spectrum primarily because:
options: It proposed the partition of India
It recommended scrapping the provincial legislatures
It had no Indian member — all seven members were British
questions.explanation: The Simon Commission was boycotted because it was an all-white, seven-member British commission with no Indian representation, tasked with reviewing constitutional reforms. Indians were enraged at being excluded from deliberations about their own governance.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: Who gave the famous slogan 'Do or Die' (Karo ya Maro) during the Quit India Movement of 1942?
questions.explanation: Gandhi gave the slogan 'Do or Die' at the AICC meeting in Bombay on August 8, 1942, urging Indians to either free India or die in the attempt. It became the rallying cry of the Quit India Movement.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The Forward Bloc, a left-leaning political party within the Congress, was founded in 1939 by:
questions.explanation: Subhas Chandra Bose founded the Forward Bloc in 1939 after he resigned from the INC presidency due to differences with Gandhi over the pace and methods of the independence struggle. The Forward Bloc called for mass agitation and complete independence.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The term 'Swaraj' as a prominent political demand in the INC platform was forcefully articulated and popularized by which leader with the declaration 'Swaraj is my birthright'?
questions.explanation: Bal Gangadhar Tilak declared 'Swaraj is my birthright, and I shall have it!' (Swarajya maza janmasiddha hakka ahe, ani to mi milavnarach). He was the first to make Swaraj a mass political demand. Dadabhai Naoroji first mentioned Swaraj in the 1906 Calcutta session.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The Poona Pact (September 1932) was a significant agreement between Gandhi (who was on a fast unto death) and:
options: B.R. Ambedkar (on behalf of Depressed Classes)
questions.explanation: The Poona Pact was signed between Gandhi and B.R. Ambedkar on September 24, 1932. It replaced the separate electorate for Depressed Classes (given by the Communal Award) with reserved seats in the general electorate. Gandhi ended his fast, and Ambedkar accepted the deal to save Gandhi's life.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: Lala Lajpat Rai died on November 17, 1928 from injuries sustained during a lathicharge while leading a protest against:
questions.explanation: Lala Lajpat Rai led the protest against the Simon Commission's arrival in Lahore on October 30, 1928, with the slogan 'Simon Go Back'. Police Superintendent J.A. Scott ordered a lathicharge; Lajpat Rai was severely beaten and died on November 17, 1928.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The Indian National Army (INA / Azad Hind Fauj) was originally organized in 1942 in Singapore among Indian POWs under Japanese captivity by:
questions.explanation: Captain Mohan Singh of the British Indian Army organized the first INA in 1942 with support from the Japanese and Indian Independence League. Rash Behari Bose (Japan-based) provided political leadership. Subhas Chandra Bose took command in 1943 and reorganized it as Azad Hind Fauj.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The Khilafat Movement (1919–22) was launched in India in support of:
options: Muslim League's demand for a separate Muslim state
The rights of Indian Muslims under British rule
The repeal of the Rowlatt Act
questions.explanation: The Khilafat Movement, led by brothers Muhammad Ali and Shaukat Ali, protested the dismemberment of the Ottoman Empire after World War I and the threat to the Caliphate (Khilafat). Gandhi supported it to forge Hindu-Muslim unity; the movement fused with the Non-Cooperation Movement.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The Civil Disobedience Movement (1930) was primarily launched to protest which specific British law/policy?
options: Salt tax (violation of the British salt monopoly)
questions.explanation: Gandhi chose the salt tax as the central issue — salt was taxed by the British even though it was available freely in nature, making it a symbol of unjust colonial exploitation affecting every Indian. The Dandi March and manufacturing of salt at Dandi launched the Civil Disobedience Movement.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The Indian Independence Act, which provided for the partition of India into two dominions, received Royal Assent on:
questions.explanation: The Indian Independence Act 1947 was passed by the British Parliament and received Royal Assent on July 18, 1947. June 3 was the Mountbatten Plan announcement; August 15 was the formal Independence Day.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The partition of Bengal in 1905 was carried out by which Viceroy of India?
questions.explanation: Viceroy Lord Curzon partitioned Bengal in October 1905, dividing it into East Bengal (with Assam, Muslim-majority) and West Bengal (Hindu-majority). The partition sparked the Swadeshi Movement and was annulled by Lord Hardinge in 1911 at the Delhi Durbar.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The popular slogan 'Lal-Bal-Pal' refers to which trio of leaders of the Extremist faction in the Indian independence movement?
options: Lala Lajpat Rai, Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Bipin Chandra Pal
Lal Bahadur Shastri, Balwantrao Mehta, Pitamber Pant
Lala Har Dayal, Balraj Madhok, Pattabhi Sitaramayya
Three Gandhian leaders of the Champaran movement
questions.explanation: Lal-Bal-Pal refers to Lala Lajpat Rai (Punjab), Bal Gangadhar Tilak (Maharashtra), and Bipin Chandra Pal (Bengal) — the trio who led the Extremist wing of the INC and championed Swaraj, Swadeshi, Boycott, and National Education as the four-point programme.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about the Non-Cooperation Movement (1920–22) is INCORRECT?
options: It was called off following the Chauri Chaura incident
It included the boycott of foreign goods and legislative councils
It ended with the Gandhi-Irwin Pact of 1931
questions.explanation: The Gandhi-Irwin Pact (1931) ended the Civil Disobedience Movement, NOT the Non-Cooperation Movement. The Non-Cooperation Movement was suspended by Gandhi in February 1922 after the Chauri Chaura incident, where a mob burned a police station killing 22 policemen.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The Chauri Chaura incident (February 5, 1922), which led Gandhi to call off the Non-Cooperation Movement, occurred in which present-day state?
questions.explanation: Chauri Chaura is a town in Gorakhpur district of present-day Uttar Pradesh. An angry mob burned down a police chowki (station), killing 22 policemen. Gandhi viewed this violence as a betrayal of non-violent principles and called off the Non-Cooperation Movement.
questions.subject: History
